sonnet.problem: The card says "The Lord says" before the quote from Isaiah 3:4. The verse puts the words in quotation marks but doesn't say who is speaking. The card names a speaker the text doesn't name. Card 5 makes the same attribution: "the Lord says He will put kings…".
sonnet.rule: When the text doesn't say who is speaking, he doesn't guess. He uses a plain lead-in, like "Then the psalm says…", and names a speaker only when the passage or its heading does.

sonnet.problem: Cards 8 and 9 both ask about Isaiah 3:11. The first asks what is coming for the wicked ("disaster is upon them"), and the second asks about being "repaid with what their hands have done". Both lines make the same point, so they should be one question. The fill-in-the-blank answer "hands" also depends on wording the baker hasn't seen.
sonnet.rule: Two lines that make the same point get one question.
